Requirements: The Certificate in Literary Translation is for students already enrolled in a graduate program (M.A. or Ph.D.) at Indiana University. [10] Students must inform the chair of the Translation Studies committee of their intent to complete the certificate. The requirements include 21-24 credit hours of coursework, including C580 (History and Theory of Translation), two translation workshops, and three other relevant graduate-level courses. [9] Applicants must have expert knowledge of English and another language. A final, substantial translation project of a literary or scholarly work into English, typically 40-60 pages long and accompanied by an explanatory essay, is also required. [9]
Description: The Certificate in Literary Translation testifies to a complete course of study in the practice and theory of literary translation. As a complement to a graduate qualification in comparative literature or any other area of study, the certificate offers a clear advantage to students in a complex and multilingual world. [2] The certificate program requires a seminar in translation theory and workshops in the practice of literary translation, as well as advanced graduate work in another language department. [2] Certificate students collaborate with faculty and the translation studies committee to complete and present a substantial project. This entails the translation of a literary or scholarly work into English along with an essay addressing the theoretical and practical issues salient in the translation process. [2, 3] The program comprises 21-24 credits. [3]

Requirements: Applicants for the Doctor of Philosophy in Media Arts and Sciences are expected to hold a four-year bachelor's degree and a two-year master's degree or a comparable credential from an accredited institution, with a minimum GPA of 3.5 in their master's program or its equivalent. [1] Three letters of recommendation are also necessary for the application. [1, 2]

Concentration: Students earning a Ph.D. in Mathematical Sciences have the option to specialize in pure mathematics, applied mathematics or mathematical statistics. [2, 8]
Description: ThePh. D. in Mathematical Sciences is offered in the Department of Mathematical Sciences. Students earning aPh. D. in Mathematical Sciences have the option to specialize in pure mathematics, applied mathematics or mathematical statistics. Our department is currently doing research in integrable systems, mathematical physics, dynamical systems, noncommutative geometry, operator algebras, differential geometry, partial differential equations, functional analysis, statistics and probability, applied mathematics, biomathematics, computational neurosciences, and scientific computing. [2]

ProgramName: Mathematics Education (Ed.D. in Curriculum and Instruction, Online)
Description: The 60-credit, post-masters Ed. D. degree is for experienced mathematics teachers, instructional leaders, and others wishing to pursue a doctorate focusing on mathematics education. [1] This fully online program offers flexibility for working professionals from across the U.S. and around the world. [1] Courses are taught by world-renowned mathematics education faculty. [1] As a student in the Ed.D. in Curriculum and Instruction with a specialization in mathematics education, you'll develop the skills you need to work in a variety of educational domains, such as research, teacher education, and curriculum development. [2] This program allows you to learn new strategies for engaging students—from problem-based, discussion-rich teaching methods to appropriate uses of technology in math classrooms. [2] Courses focus on: effective mathematics teaching, mathematical thinking and learning, equity in mathematics education, mathematics curriculum, problem solving, teaching mathematics with digital technologies, mathematics assessment, and mathematics teacher education. [1, 2]
Accredidation: Requires a Bachelor's degree and a Master's degree from an accredited institution. [1, 2]

ProgramName: Mathematics Education (Ph.D. in Curriculum and Instruction)
Requirements: A completed online application is required which includes a Personal statement, Resume, and two letters of recommendation. A Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a minimum accumulative GPA of 2.75 out of 4.00 is necessary. GRE scores are required. For international students, a minimum TOEFL score of 79, a minimum IELTS score of 6.5, or a minimum Duolingo score of 115 is required. [7]
Description: The Ph.D. prepares students to do research and teach mathematics and mathematics education at colleges and universities. Specifically, this 90-credit hour Ph.D. program prepares you to conduct original research on topics in Mathematics Education, such as studies on how students and teachers learn mathematics, examinations of equity in mathematics education, assessments of students' and teachers' mathematical knowledge, studies about teachers' beliefs, and studies about how technology can be used to enhance mathematics learning. The doctoral program focuses on K-12 mathematics teaching and learning. [4] Most students entering the program have K-12 teaching experience, and graduates of the program often become university faculty who prepare elementary and secondary teachers. [4]

Requirements: While there are no absolute prerequisites for admission, the most important credential is a record of successful work in advanced mathematics courses. Most successful applicants have an undergraduate degree in mathematics or a closely related field. A successful applicant will normally have completed courses in advanced calculus, linear algebra, and modern algebra.
Description: Students in the Master of Science in Applied Statistics degree program learn the basis for the application of modern statistical methods. In addition to the basic theoretical foundations, areas of methodology include regression analysis, design of experiments, multivariate analysis, quality control, survival analysis, time series, sample surveys, categorical, and nonparametric methodology. All applied courses use and emphasize the importance of modern statistical computing software. You'll learn to use a broad base of practical techniques and applications from a wide variety of fields. At the same time the student's background in theory is developed so the learning process will continue in any professional environment pursued after graduation. You'll graduate with broad training in statistical methodology that is suitable for applications in industry, medicine, business and government.

Concentration: The official Indiana University websites do not specify a distinct concentration name for the general Master of Science in Medical and Molecular Genetics program. However, the program does offer a specific track or plan in 'Genetic Counseling'. [4]
Description: The Master of Science in Medical and Molecular Genetics is an independent degree designed to prepare students for careers in laboratory research or education. [1, 3] Students must complete a minimum of 30 credit hours of approved coursework with at least a 3.0 GPA. [1] The curriculum includes at least 20 hours in Medical Genetics or approved equivalents, with required courses such as Basic Human Genetics, Clinical Genetics, Molecular and Biochemical Genetics, Human Cytogenetics, and Population Genetics. [1] Students completing the research-focused Master of Science will be able to demonstrate an in-depth understanding of medical and molecular genetics, integrate biological knowledge from various approaches, critically analyze scientific literature, and present scientific ideas. [4] For the degree completion, students have the option to either prepare and defend a Master's thesis, have a first-authorship on a refereed publication with departmental approval, or complete an additional six hours of non-research coursework. [1]
Accredidation: The official Indiana University websites do not mention a specific accreditation for the Master of Science in Medical and Molecular Genetics program itself. However, it is noted that the laboratories within the Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics are accredited by the College of American Pathologists (CAP) and certified by CLIA. [7] The related Clinical Genetics Residency program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME). [2]

Concentration: ['MD dual degree programs allow medical students to adjust the traditional four-year MD education schedule to complete coursework for a PhD, MBA, JD, MPH, MS or MA.', 'Scholarly Concentrations and certificate programs']
Description: Indiana University School of Medicine offers a nationally recognized, fully accredited four-year medical education program leading to a Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree. The MD program at IU School of Medicine is the largest undergraduate medical education program in the United States. [12] With nine campuses and strong partnerships with teaching hospitals throughout the state, the school offers unparalleled opportunities and resources for students to explore their interests and pursue specialty training to prepare for successful careers. [12] After students complete this phase of medical education, they often match to highly desirable residency programs — either at IU School of Medicine or other competitive medical schools — to continue training. The four years of medical school are divided into three phases. The first two years focus on the basic sciences with clinical integration; the third- and fourth-years are devoted solely to clinical experiences with emphasis on specialty training for career placement in the fourth year. [12] Required third-year clerkships include eight-week rotations in Internal Medicine, Pediatrics and Surgery; four-week rotations in Family Medicine, Neurology, OB/Gyn and Psychiatry; and a two-week rotation in Anesthesia. [12] Fourth year electives provide students the flexibility to pursue focused training in specific areas of medicine. [12]
Accredidation: The Doctor of Medicine (MD) program at Indiana University School of Medicine is fully accredited. [12] The accrediting body for MD programs in the United States is the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME). [2, 17]

The evidence-based curriculum and practical training spans prevalence, prevention, and treatment of substance use disorders. Through a combination of coursework, laboratory experiences, practica, and internships you'll develop effective counseling skills and gain the qualifications and confidence needed to help others. [1]

Description: The Master of Science (MS) degree program in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology prepares research scientists for productive careers at a highly competitive level in the ever-changing health care market place. [4] The department offers didactic coursework sufficient for rapid mastery of concepts central to the discipline while emphasizing active student involvement in the laboratory as quickly as possible. [4] Students are engaged in ongoing accrual of knowledge and accomplishments in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology through attendance at the weekly departmental seminar, participation in the weekly departmental research in progress meeting, participation in journal clubs and research meetings and attendance and presentations at local and national meetings. [4] The program provides varied forums to enhance student communication and teaching skills and expects training to be completed in two to three years, producing independent, creative investigators. [4]

Requirements: Admission to the MELC Ph.D. requires a BA or MA in an appropriate field with at least a 3.0 GPA. Any student whose first language is not English (including dual U.S. citizens who were educated in a language other than English) must submit a Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) score of at least 79, or an International English Language Testing Service (IELTS) score of at least 6.5. The Graduate Record Exam is not required for any applicant. [2]
Department: Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies
Concentration: Students will select one of the following three MELC core areas as their primary field: Arabic Language and Linguistics; Islamic Studies and Pre-Modern Middle Eastern Cultures; or the Modern Middle East. [5]
Description: The Department of Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures is affiliated with the Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies (HLS) in the College of Arts and Sciences, dedicated to providing Indiana University graduate students with the intellectual tools they will need to live, work, and thrive in the globalized world of the twenty-first century. [5] The Ph.D. in Middle Eastern Languages & Cultures at HLS allows students to work with renowned IU faculty and prepares them for an academic career at the university or college level. [4] Graduates develop a strong language foundation and expertise in this critical region of the world. [4] Developing language expertise is a core part of the Ph.D. program, requiring three non-English languages: a major MELC language (normally Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish), a minor MELC language, and a European research language. [4] The Ph.D. program culminates in written and oral exams, as well as a dissertation. [4]
CostPerCredit: $644.52 per credit hour for Indiana residents, $1,863.32 per credit hour for non-residents (2023-2024 rates, subject to change)

Requirements: The application process for doctoral programs at the Jacobs School of Music requires applicants to complete both the Indiana University Graduate School application and the Jacobs School of Music Supplemental Application. [8] General requirements include the submission of academic materials such as transcripts from previous institutions and three letters of recommendation. [8] An audition and/or interview is also required, with specific requirements varying by department. [8] Applicants whose native language is not English must submit a TOEFL or IELTS score, with a minimum TOEFL score of 100 (internet-based) or an IELTS score of 7.5 for doctoral applicants. [8]

All new applicants to a graduate program must apply online to both the Indiana University Graduate School and to the Jacobs School of Music. [5] Applicants to all graduate degree and diploma programs are evaluated based on an audition and/or interview. [5] The application process includes providing email addresses for three recommenders who will receive a secure link to upload their letters. [1] Academic materials such as transcripts are also required. [1] For admission to a master's degree program, a minimum TOEFL score of 84 (Internet-based) or an IELTS score of 6.5 is required for applicants whose native language is not English. [5]
ScholarshipType: Graduate Tuition Award, Artistic Excellence Award, Jacobs Fellowship, endowed scholarships, Associate Instructorships, and Graduate Assistantships

Description: The Indiana University School of Nursing offers a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) with two tracks: Clinical Nurse Specialist and Nurse Educator. The program is designed for those interested in a career in either of these roles and is taught by nationally-recognized faculty. While based out of the IU Indianapolis campus, most courses are offered online or in a hybrid-distance format. Clinical and practicum experiences can be completed within the student's home community in Indiana and are arranged collaboratively between students and faculty. The program's learning outcomes focus on several domains, including Knowledge for Nursing Practice, Person-Centered Care, Population Health, Scholarship for the Nursing Discipline, Quality and Safety, Systems-Based Practice, and Informatics and Healthcare Technologies.
Accredidation: All of our bachelor's, master's, and Doctor of Nursing Practice programs are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education. [7]

Description: The Nursing Administration track prepares registered nurses for advanced management and leadership positions in a variety of healthcare settings such as hospitals, clinics, surgery centers, and community agencies. [1, 8] The program provides nursing professionals with a path toward advanced practice at the administrative level, focusing on pivotal roles in healthcare administration and management. [3] Students will explore leadership and decision-making processes, including financial stewardship, analysis of research and health policy, and strategic planning, to support improvements in healthcare delivery. [8] The curriculum is designed to equip nurses with advanced practice knowledge to enhance community health care and transform health care delivery systems. [1]

Fees: The total tuition for the Kelley Direct Online MBA program is $94,944 for 54 credit hours for cohorts starting in fall 2024 and spring 2025. An additional $2,000 in fees covers in-person experiences, including lodging, meals, and course materials. [9]

Requirements: Applicants for a doctorate degree at the Jacobs School of Music must apply online to both the Indiana University Graduate School and the Jacobs School of Music. A bachelor's degree and the equivalent of a master's degree in music are required for admission. The admissions committee evaluates applicants based on their past academic record, letters of recommendation, and a required audition and/or interview. Applicants whose native language is not English must submit TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Department: Department of Theatre, Drama, and Contemporary Dance

Description: The Master of Arts in Philanthropic Studies provides a comprehensive understanding of the intricate social, cultural, political, and economic dynamics that influence the philanthropic sector. [1] It is designed to be a gateway to comprehending the roles that philanthropy and nonprofit organizations play. [2] Students in the program delve into subjects such as the nonprofit and voluntary sectors, civil society, the history of philanthropy in America, and the ethical principles and values of philanthropy. [2] The curriculum is structured to help students gain experience in applying advanced research and to cultivate critical thinking skills regarding the complex challenges that the nonprofit sector faces. [4] Ultimately, the program aims to prepare graduates for leadership roles by deepening their individual leadership practices as they apply their learning. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: Grants up to $1,000 per year are available for students in the M.A. program. [23]
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, assistantships, and scholarships are available. [6]

Description: The Department of Philosophy at Indiana University offers a Ph.D. program. The curriculum for the doctoral degree includes distribution requirements across four areas: History of Philosophy, Metaphysics and Epistemology, Logic, and Value Theory. [8] Students must complete nine units of these distribution requirements. [8] For the History of Philosophy, three units are required, with at least one in ancient or medieval history and one in post-medieval history. [8] The requirement for Metaphysics and Epistemology and Logic is a disjunctive one, where students have options to fulfill the requirements in these areas. [8] The Value Theory requirement covers ethics, social and political philosophy, legal philosophy, and aesthetics. [8] The program also offers a Master of Arts degree, which requires 30 credit hours. [8]

Description: The Master of Public Affairs (MPA) Program provides education in public management and policy analysis that prepares students for careers in public policy and administration in government, private, and nonprofit sectors. [4] The award-winning La Follette School faculty includes economists, political scientists, sociologists, and public affairs scholars who teach the skills and tools needed for a career in public affairs. [4] They are experts in social policy, health policy and management, public administration, public policy analysis, environmental policy, poverty, and tax policy and government finance. [4]
Accredidation: Accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA). [2, 5, 11, 12]

Department: O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs
Description: The Public Management concentration prepares students with the strategic and technical skills needed to address the challenges and opportunities found in and surrounding government organizations. [1] The strategic and evidence-based management skills students acquire through courses in this concentration will be matched with the development of leadership skills essential to guiding organizations toward ethical and self–accountable decision making. [1] Because government increasingly works in concert with the nonprofit and private sectors to address complex public problems, such as education, healthcare, and sustainability, the Public Management concentration also provides students with management skills that will enable them to collaborate with organizations outside of the government sector. [1]
Accredidation: The O'Neill MPA program at IU Indianapolis is fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Public Affairs and Administration (NASPAA). [12]
CostPerCredit: $753.83/credit hour for Indiana residents and qualifying military/veteran students, $1,434.35/credit hour for non-residents (for the online MPA, residential rates were not specified)

Requirements: Admission to the urban education studies doctoral program is competitive and requires faculty approval. Admission is based on an applicant's qualifications, submitted application materials (including official transcripts*, resume/curriculum vitae, writing sample, personal statements, letters of recommendation), a personal interview, and references. A master's degree is required for admission to the program. [2]
Description: The doctoral program in Urban Education Studies at the IU School of Education in Indianapolis prepares students to become scholar-leaders with a critical understanding of the complexities of education in urban environments, and a strong grounding in research methodologies. [2] As a highly unique urban education studies Ph.D. program in the United States, with a faculty that is over 60% faculty of color and doctoral cohorts that average more than 60% students of color, we focus on an in-depth understanding of the complex assets and inequities within the urban education environment. [4] Upon graduation, you will have a critical understanding of the sociological and educational issues within urban education, the surrounding urban environment, the larger society, and the interactions among them. [4] You will have also developed a critical understanding of research, research methodologies, and research theories and will have the foundation for becoming an engaged scholar. [4]

The Ph.D. in Vision Science is offered to top students worldwide. With leading programs in biology, optics, imaging, and vision science, you can prepare for a career in academic or industry research while interacting each week with professionals in the field. An M.S. degree is not required for application to the Ph.D. program in Vision Science. Vision science is multidisciplinary, and can include the study of biochemistry, biophysics, engineering, epidemiology, molecular biology, cell biology, neuroscience, optics, ophthalmology, optometry, pathology, physiology, psychology, statistics, and any other discipline that relates to the eye and its problems. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Affairs
Requirements: To be considered for the Bachelor of Science in Public Affairs, applicants must first apply to Indiana University Bloomington and indicate a major within the O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs on their application. [14] The university accepts either the Apply IU Application or the Common Application. [8] A required component of the application is an IU-specific essay of 200-400 words describing the applicant's academic and career plans. [8] Admission to the O'Neill School is competitive and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis through a holistic review that considers the applicant's academic record, the quality of their application essay(s), and other activities and achievements. [14]
Department: O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs
Fees: Estimated tuition and mandatory fees for the 2026–2027 academic year are $12,142 for Indiana residents and $42,702 for non-residents. [1]
Concentration: ['Environmental Management', 'Human Resource Management', 'Law and Public Policy', 'Management', 'Nonprofit Management and Leadership', 'Policy Analysis', 'Public Financial Management', 'Public Management and Leadership']
Description: Whether you're interested in launching a career on Capitol Hill, learning how to manage and motivate people, or protecting the planet, a Bachelor of Science in Public Affairs (BSPA) degree equips you with the skills to make a difference. With the O'Neill School's core public affairs coursework, you'll study the basics of policymaking, budgeting, and finance. You'll also pick a major and develop leadership and analytical skills that can be applied to your specific area of interest.
ScholarshipAmount: The IU Foundation offers scholarships typically ranging from $1,000 to $2,000 annually. [14] The O'Neill School provides scholarships with award amounts between $500 and $15,000 per year. [25]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science
Requirements: To apply to Indiana University, applicants must be on track to earn an accredited high school diploma or equivalent. [1] The application for admission requires an essay. [8] General application requirements include the online application, academic records, and an application fee. [7]
Department: O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs and College of Arts + Sciences
Description: With a major in Environmental Science through a Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science (BSES) degree, you will study the environment and look for solutions to pressing environmental problems. You'll also have opportunities to study abroad in places like South Korea, South Africa, Portugal, and Costa Rica. The BSES is a joint degree program between the O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs and the College of Arts + Sciences—to offer you a selection of courses on a wide range of environmental topics, taught by over 40 faculty and instructors across Indiana University. You'll follow an interdisciplinary approach, gaining knowledge and tools from the traditional sciences, such as biology, chemistry, geology, hydrology, mathematics, meteorology, and physics. [5] Many of the courses include field and laboratory work, providing valuable hands-on experience, and demonstrating the applied nature of environmental science. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental and Sustainability Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Environmental and Sustainability Studies, prospective students must apply for undergraduate admission to Indiana University. The program is a joint degree between the O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs and the College of Arts and Sciences. For specific admission information, prospective students are advised to contact the BAESS advisor. [8] General application is done through the Common Application.
Department: College of Arts and Sciences and the O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs. [25]
Concentration: ['sustainable food systems', 'sustainable energy and resources', 'environmental ethics and justice', 'biodiversity and sustainability', 'an individualized concentration']
Description: If sustainability, human-environment interactions, sustainable food systems, and environmental ethics topics intrigue you, a Bachelor of Arts in Environmental and Sustainability Studies (BAESS) degree—which is also a major in environmental and sustainability studies—will give you the opportunity to study these subjects and more. [1] With a BAESS, you will gain a broad overview of environmental sustainability problems and the tools needed to address these issues. [1] You'll also have opportunities to explore sustainability globally by studying abroad in places like South Africa, Portugal, or Costa Rica. [1] The Bachelor of Arts in Environmental and Sustainability Studies is an interdisciplinary, liberal-arts degree designed to provide an introduction to the complex system-scale challenges of sustainability as well as the tools needed to address problems that transcend solely social or environmental domains. [4] Students pursuing this degree can expect to integrate experience in the humanities with the natural and social sciences. [4] The major offers the opportunity to develop skills in communication and creative expression, data collection and analysis, environmental science, and economics. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Arts Management
Requirements: To be considered for admission to Indiana University Bloomington, all applicants must have an accredited high school diploma or its equivalent. [5] While there's no set minimum GPA, the majority of admitted students have a GPA between 3.5 and 4.0. [2] The university takes a holistic approach, considering factors like the rigor of high school coursework, extracurricular activities, and a required personal essay that provides insight into your academic and personal goals. [1, 2] Letters of recommendation are also encouraged. [2]
Department: O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs
Description: Study the behind-the-scenes elements of the arts world, including arts marketing, finance, nonprofit management, and law. You'll learn the fundamentals of running an arts organization while specializing in a specific arts area tailored to your interests and career goals. You'll also have opportunities to explore global approaches to arts management by studying abroad in places like Switzerland, Scotland, or the Netherlands. You'll complete an internship in the area you're studying—whether that's with a record label in Nashville or at a museum in the nation's capital—and graduate with real-world experience and a head start on your career. [1]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships such as the O'Neill Scholars Award and the Boch Family Scholarship are available.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Healthcare Management and Policy
Requirements: General admission to Indiana University is the first step. For direct admission to the O'Neill School, which houses the program, incoming freshmen can be admitted with a 3.3 high school GPA (test-optional). Alternatively, students with a 3.0 high school GPA and an SAT score of 1000+ or an ACT composite score of 21 can be directly admitted. [4] Students who do not meet these criteria are admitted to University College and can transfer to O'Neill after their first semester if they have declared an O'Neill major and earned a 2.0 cumulative GPA. [4]
Department: O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs
Fees: $12,144 for in-state students and $41,891 for out-of-state students for the 2024-25 academic year.
Description: Study the complex economic and political factors affecting an issue that is critical to all of us—our health. In the Bachelor of Science in Healthcare Management and Policy program, you'll be taught by nationally known faculty as well as practitioners who understand the issues firsthand: Learn healthcare law from practicing attorneys, long-term care from the administrator of a 300-bed facility, and strategic planning from a hospital CEO. You'll graduate with the leadership skills necessary to ensure people have access to the health services they need—and the analytical skills to reform healthcare from the inside out. [5]
CostPerCredit: $392 per credit hour for in-state undergraduates, $1,112 per credit hour for out-of-state students.

Requirements: To be considered for direct admission to the Kelley School of Business for a Bachelor of Science in Accounting, first-year applicants must submit their IU Bloomington application by the November 1 early action deadline, indicating a Kelley business major. [1] Applicants must also complete the Kelley Prospect Inventory (KPI) through the IU Admissions Portal. [1] There are no automatic criteria for direct admission; all applicants who submit the KPI will undergo a comprehensive academic review that considers factors such as high school performance, the rigor of high school coursework, academic achievements, and potential for success at the Kelley School. [1]
Description: Year after year, the Kelley School's Bachelor of Science in Business (B.S.B.) in Accounting is ranked one of the best programs in the nation. In fact, U.S. News & World Report Best Undergraduate Business Programs 2024 ranks this program at No. 4. This degree could be a great fit for students who enjoy math, are skilled communicators, and a good at solving problems. With an undergraduate degree from the Kelley School of Business, you'll be able to: analyze and interpret the economic, social, political, legal, cultural, and technological influences that drive the global economy, evaluate a region or nation for business investment or expansion, and develop a comprehensive knowledge base in each essential division of business and understand the important relationships among finance, marketing, operations, and leadership. In addition, accounting majors acquire the tools for intelligent analysis, planning, control, and decision-making. Students learn to address the oral and written skills accounting professionals need in order to be effective team members and serve clients well.

Requirements: To apply for freshman admission at Indiana University, prospective students must submit an application via the Common Application or the Apply IU application. As part of the application, an essay is required. [2, 7] The curriculum includes courses in the arts, sciences, and humanities as part of the general education requirements. [2] Students will gain knowledge in core business disciplines such as economics, human resources, international business, commercial law, new venture creation, and consumer behavior. [7] The program at IU Online, for instance, provides a broad foundation in high-demand fields like economics, management, quantitative business analysis, finance, marketing, and information systems. [11] At IU Southeast, the general business concentration offers a comprehensive understanding of fundamental business concepts spanning finance, marketing, management, and operations. [18] The program at IU Northwest starts with a broad foundation and then allows students to focus their advanced coursework in a concentration that aligns with their career interests. [2]

Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree in Biology trains students in the major subject areas of biology a remaining the most flexible of all biology degrees offered. Minimal chemistry and mathematics requirements allow you to substitute a second major, such as computer science, chemistry, psychology, environmental studies, or business. Because of its flexibility, this degree is ideal for students who wish to pursue a second major, combining the study of biology with another subject area. If you want the flexibility to explore other academic disciplines, wish to teach middle school or high school biology, or desire to work in business, the Biology B.A. degree may be a good option for you. Your work in the major begins with two courses—Foundations of Biology: Diversity, Evolution, and Ecology and Foundations of Biology: Biological Mechanisms. Lab work and courses in molecular biology, genetics, and evolution are also required. Additional lecture courses and lab work enable you to complete the degree. [2]

Candidates for this program are considered generalists, taking a range of content courses, professional foundation courses, and methods courses that cover the various subject areas taught in elementary schools. The program is designed to equip teacher education candidates with the skills to teach all subjects to children from kindergarten through sixth grade. Students gain a broad background in English, mathematics, humanities, social sciences, and the sciences, which is complemented by classes on teaching methods. A significant part of the curriculum includes multiple field experiences in elementary schools, allowing students to practice and improve their teaching abilities. [1, 4, 9]

[14] History students learn how change takes place, the tensions and conflicts it causes, and how individuals, groups, and societies change over time. [14] Students develop skills and tools for retrieving and interpreting the past and, in the process, for better understanding the questions and challenges of our own time. [14] Courses cover a wide range of issues in all time periods and parts of the world. [14]

The B.A. is designed to be paired with other areas of interest, with Economics being a popular double major.

We also provide training in the fundamental principles of neuroscience and opportunities for more advanced training in specific topics in the field. In our program, you will gain a deep understanding of neuroscience, from the cellular and molecular bases of nervous system function to a systems-level approach to the study of brain-behavior relationships.

[6] Courses in the department emphasize clear and cogent thinking about fundamental problems, locate the origins of these problems in the writings of the great philosophers, and provide in-depth examinations of proposed solutions. [6] The major is flexible enough to meet the needs of those planning to become professional philosophers as well as those with other career goals. [6] Students will develop skills in identifying and critically evaluating arguments, thinking clearly and independently, writing analytically, and applying principles of logic and good reasoning. [7, 9, 10] They will also gain an understanding of the history of Western Philosophy and fundamental issues regarding central philosophical topics, learning to develop and defend their own philosophical views. [7, 9, 10] The program fosters an open-minded, non-dogmatic attitude and the ability to tolerate uncertainty. [7, 10]

Description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Physics at Indiana University is a versatile degree preparing students for immediate employment or for advanced studies in physics or related scientific and medical fields. [10] The curriculum covers the foundations of physics, including classical mechanics, classical electrodynamics, quantum mechanics, relativity, and statistical physics, fostering rigorous and analytical thinking. [3] Students are encouraged to participate in research and can choose from programs in optical physics, solid state physics, or biological physics, culminating in a capstone experience in a physics research laboratory. [3] The program is designed to develop problem-solving skills and provides a strong foundation for various careers, including patent law, medicine, and finance, as physicists have been fundamental in inventing technologies like electric motors, lasers, and medical imaging systems. [3] Although there is a single B.S. in Physics, the department provides strong recommendations for elective choices through different "tracks" based on a student's career goals. [10]

Radiographers are essential members of the healthcare team. They are experts in the performance of examinations requiring the use of X-rays and highly complex machinery to produce a quality X-ray image (radiograph) of the internal parts of the body for interpretation by a medical doctor (radiologist). Description: Students of creative writing tap into the basic human desire to tell stories—to learn about the experiences of others while sharing their own and building bridges across differences. [6] Creative writers learn how to use language to express their unique ideas, opinions, and perspectives through poetry and prose. [6] Students of creative writing add their unique voices to a centuries-old literary discussion, learning from, and responding to, the writers and traditions of the past while forging new paths forward. [6] Students of creative writing learn how to read as writers—studying what makes writing successful and using those tools to craft their own original work. [6] Creative writers learn to think critically both on and off the page, questioning assumptions, engaging in dialogue, and coming to—and sharing—their own original conclusions in language that lingers and resonates. [6] Students of creative writing are exposed to cultures, world views, religions, and perspectives far beyond their own as they explore written texts from around the world, gaining new insight, understanding, and awareness. [6] Creative writers actively engage in the politics, challenges, and questions that affect our world now. [6] Creative writers learn how to represent themselves articulately and effectively in both written and spoken language—skills that will serve you well no matter your chosen major! [6] Students of creative writing give themselves the time and opportunity to create—to make something new and meaningful, changing the world by adding their own artistic mark. [6] The creative writing students of today are the writers to be studied tomorrow. [6]
